title: Judges Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 3.

questions.question: Which nations did the LORD leave to prove Israel according to Judges 3?
options: Five lords of the Philistines, Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivites
questions.correctAnswer: Five lords of the Philistines, Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivites
questions.explanation: Judges 3:3 lists these nations specifically as those the LORD left to prove Israel.

questions.question: Why did the LORD leave certain nations alive among Israel?
options: To teach Israel to make peace
To prove Israel and teach them war
To force Israel to worship those nations’ gods
questions.correctAnswer: To prove Israel and teach them war
questions.explanation: Judges 3:1-2 explains that the LORD left these nations to prove Israel and teach those who had no knowledge of war.

questions.question: According to Judges 3, which command did Israel have to hearken unto?
options: Commands given by the LORD through Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Commands given by the LORD through Moses
questions.explanation: Judges 3:4 states that the test was to see if Israel would obey the commandments given by the LORD through Moses.

questions.question: With which peoples did the children of Israel dwell, according to Judges 3:5?
options: Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
questions.correctAnswer: Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
questions.explanation: Judges 3:5 specifically lists these peoples among whom Israel dwelt.

questions.question: What evil did the children of Israel do in the sight of the LORD in Judges 3?
options: They forgot the LORD and served Baalim and the groves
questions.correctAnswer: They forgot the LORD and served Baalim and the groves
questions.explanation: Judges 3:7 states that Israel did evil by forgetting the LORD and serving Baalim and the groves.

questions.question: Who was the king of Mesopotamia that the LORD sold Israel into because of their evil?
questions.correctAnswer: Chushanrishathaim
questions.explanation: Judges 3:8 identifies Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia as the one whom Israel served for eight years.

questions.question: How long did Israel serve Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia?
questions.correctAnswer: Eight years
questions.explanation: Judges 3:8 states that Israel served Chushanrishathaim for eight years.

questions.question: Who was raised up by the LORD as a deliverer to free Israel from Mesopotamia?
questions.correctAnswer: Othniel
questions.explanation: Judges 3:9 shows that the LORD raised up Othniel, Caleb's younger brother, to deliver Israel.

questions.question: What special empowerment did Othniel receive to judge Israel and go to war?
options: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him
He was given a mighty army by Moses
He received a sword from Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him
questions.explanation: Judges 3:10 states that the Spirit of the LORD came upon Othniel enabling him to judge and fight.

questions.question: How many years of rest did the land have after Othniel’s deliverance?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: Judges 3:11 states the land had rest for forty years after Othniel died.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD sold Israel into the hand of Eglon, king of Moab, because Israel had done evil in His sight.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 3:12 clearly says the LORD strengthened Eglon against Israel because they did evil.

questions.question: True or False: Othniel was the son of Kenaz and the older brother of Caleb.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 3:9 states Othniel was Caleb’s younger brother, not older.

questions.question: True or False: Israel served Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia for eighteen years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 3:8 states Israel served him for eight years, not eighteen.

questions.question: True or False: The nations left by the LORD to prove Israel included the Hivites dwelling in mount Lebanon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 3:3 mentions the Hivites dwelling in mount Lebanon among the nations left to prove Israel.

questions.question: In Judges 3, which event occurs first?
options: Israel serves Eglon king of Moab
The LORD raises up Othniel to deliver Israel
Israel takes daughters of Canaanites as wives
questions.correctAnswer: Israel takes daughters of Canaanites as wives
questions.explanation: Judges 3:6 describes Israel taking Canaanite daughters as wives before the raising up of deliverers or serving other kings.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Judges 3:12, why did the LORD strengthen Eglon the king of Moab against Israel?
options: Because Israel had done evil in the sight of the LORD
Because Israel had prayed for deliverance
Because Israel obeyed the LORD's commandments
Because Eglon was a righteous king
questions.correctAnswer: Because Israel had done evil in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 3:12 states that Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD, and as a result, the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against them. This shows the consequence of disobedience to God.

questions.question: What nations did Eglon gather to help him smite Israel according to Judges 3:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Ammon and Amalek
questions.explanation: Judges 3:13 clearly states that Eglon gathered the children of Ammon and Amalek to smite Israel and take the city of palm trees, showing the coalition formed against Israel.

questions.question: How long did the children of Israel serve Eglon king of Moab as noted in Judges 3:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighteen years
questions.explanation: Judges 3:14 specifies that Israel served Eglon for eighteen years, indicating a prolonged period of oppression due to their disobedience.

questions.question: Based on Judges 3:15, who was raised up by the LORD as a deliverer for Israel?
options: Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite
questions.correctAnswer: Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite
questions.explanation: Judges 3:15 reveals that the LORD raised up Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, as a deliverer after Israel cried out for help, showing God's faithfulness to rescue His people.

questions.question: How did Ehud conceal his weapon when he went to present a gift to Eglon, according to Judges 3:16?
options: He girded a two-edged dagger under his raiment on his right thigh
He carried a sword openly in his hand
He hid a spear in his cloak
He wore armor with hidden knives
questions.correctAnswer: He girded a two-edged dagger under his raiment on his right thigh
questions.explanation: Judges 3:16 describes Ehud making a two-edged dagger and hiding it under his clothing on his right thigh, demonstrating cunning and preparation for deliverance.

questions.question: What physical description of King Eglon is provided in Judges 3:17?
options: He was a very fat man
He was blind in one eye
He was lame in one foot
questions.correctAnswer: He was a very fat man
questions.explanation: Judges 3:17 explicitly states that Eglon was a very fat man, which is key to understanding how Ehud was able to conceal the dagger and kill him.

questions.question: What was the significance of Ehud saying he had a secret errand to King Eglon in Judges 3:19?
options: It caused Eglon's attendants to leave, giving Ehud a private moment with the king
It was a request to negotiate peace
It was an announcement of tribute
It was a call for a public meeting
questions.correctAnswer: It caused Eglon's attendants to leave, giving Ehud a private moment with the king
questions.explanation: Judges 3:19 shows that Ehud's claim of a secret errand caused all attendants to leave so he could be alone with the king, enabling Ehud to carry out his plan.

questions.question: In Judges 3:20, where was King Eglon when Ehud approached him, and what did Ehud claim?
options: Sitting in a summer parlour alone; Ehud said he had a message from God
In the palace courtyard; Ehud said he was a messenger
In the city gate; Ehud claimed to bring tribute
In a temple; Ehud said he came to pray
questions.correctAnswer: Sitting in a summer parlour alone; Ehud said he had a message from God
questions.explanation: Judges 3:20 states Eglon was alone in a summer parlour when Ehud told him he had a message from God, prompting the king to rise, which facilitated Ehud’s attack.

questions.question: According to Judges 3:21-22, what prevented Ehud from drawing the dagger out after stabbing Eglon?
options: The fat closed upon the blade so tightly that it could not be drawn out
Eglon grabbed the dagger and held it
The dagger broke inside Eglon's belly
Ehud purposely left it in to cause more pain
questions.correctAnswer: The fat closed upon the blade so tightly that it could not be drawn out
questions.explanation: Verses 21 and 22 explain that Ehud stabbed Eglon with his left hand, and the fat of the king's belly closed tightly around the blade, preventing its removal.

questions.question: What was the immediate reaction of Eglon's servants when they found the parlour doors locked in Judges 3:24-25?
options: They assumed he was covering his feet and delayed opening the door
They immediately broke down the door
They called for Ehud to come back
They reported to the army that the king was safe
questions.correctAnswer: They assumed he was covering his feet and delayed opening the door
questions.explanation: Judges 3:24-25 describes the servants waiting and assuming the king was covering his feet, which delayed their discovery that Eglon was dead behind the locked door.

questions.question: How does the story of Ehud in Judges 3 teach about the virtue of faith and trust in God during difficult times?
options: It shows that God raises up deliverers when His people cry out in faith and repentance
It implies that earthly weapons and cunning alone bring victory
It emphasizes self-reliance rather than prayer
It suggests waiting passively for enemies to leave
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that God raises up deliverers when His people cry out in faith and repentance
questions.explanation: Judges 3:15 and 3:20 together show that when Israel cried to the LORD, God raised Ehud as a deliverer, illustrating the importance of faith and trusting God for rescue in hardship.

questions.question: What does Judges 3:28-29 teach about obedience to God's command through Ehud's leadership?
options: Obedience leads to victory over enemies and deliverance
It causes division among the Israelites
It brings about compromise with enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience leads to victory over enemies and deliverance
questions.explanation: Judges 3:28-29 shows that when Israel followed Ehud's command, God delivered their enemies into their hands, resulting in the killing of about ten thousand Moabites and rest for the land.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 3:22 describes that the dirt coming out was from the wound caused by Ehud's dagger.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 3:22 mentions that after Ehud thrust the dagger into Eglon's belly, the dirt came out, indicating the severity of the stabbing wound.

questions.question: True or False: According to Judges 3:18, Ehud sent away the people who bore the present before he executed his plan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 3:18 states that after Ehud finished delivering the present to Eglon, he sent away the people who bore the present, allowing him to be alone with the king for his secret errand.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 3:31 tells us that Shamgar killed 600 men with a spear.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 3:31 says Shamgar slew 600 men with an ox goad, not a spear, highlighting his unusual weapon of deliverance.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 3.

questions.question: What action did Ehud take immediately after killing King Eglon?
options: He fled through the porch and locked the doors of the parlour behind him
He called for the Israelite army to attack immediately
He hid the dagger in the palace
He proclaimed himself king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He fled through the porch and locked the doors of the parlour behind him
questions.explanation: Judges 3:23 states that after killing Eglon, Ehud went forth through the porch and shut and locked the doors of the parlour upon him to delay discovery of the murder.

questions.question: What did the servants think when they found the doors to the parlour locked after Eglon had been killed?
options: Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber
He had gone out to meet Ehud
He was praying to his gods
He had fallen asleep at his desk
questions.correctAnswer: Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber
questions.explanation: Judges 3:24 explains that the servants, seeing the locked doors, assumed their lord was covering his feet in his summer chamber, not suspecting he was dead.

questions.question: How long did the children of Israel serve Eglon, king of Moab?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighteen years
questions.explanation: Judges 3:14 states that Israel served Eglon for eighteen years because of their evil in the sight of the LORD.

questions.question: What was the unique physical characteristic of Ehud mentioned in the text?
options: He was blind in one eye
questions.correctAnswer: He was left-handed
questions.explanation: Judges 3:15 identifies Ehud as a man left-handed, which was significant in his ability to conceal his dagger on his right thigh.

questions.question: Which weapon did Shamgar use to deliver Israel, according to Judges 3?
questions.correctAnswer: An ox goad
questions.explanation: Judges 3:31 records that Shamgar slew six hundred Philistines with an ox goad, an agricultural tool, demonstrating a remarkable deliverance.

questions.question: After killing Eglon, Ehud blew a trumpet on which mountain to rally the Israelites?
questions.correctAnswer: Mountain of Ephraim
questions.explanation: Judges 3:27 says that Ehud blew a trumpet on the mountain of Ephraim, summoning the Israelites to follow him against Moab.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the battle when Israel attacked the Moabites following Ehud’s leadership?
options: About ten thousand Moabite men were slain with no survivors
The Israelites were defeated and fled
The Moabites captured the city of palm trees again
A truce was made between Israel and Moab
questions.correctAnswer: About ten thousand Moabite men were slain with no survivors
questions.explanation: Judges 3:29 confirms that about ten thousand valiant Moabite men were killed, leaving no survivors, showing a decisive victory.

questions.question: What was the length of peace in Israel after Ehud's deliverance?
questions.correctAnswer: Fourscore (eighty) years
questions.explanation: Judges 3:30 states that after Moab was subdued, the land had rest for fourscore years, indicating a long period of peace.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the narrative of Ehud’s assassination of King Eglon and the subsequent rescue of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The narrative structure in Judges 3:20–28 shows a chiasm where the story centers on Ehud’s secret message and assassination, with parallel elements before and after, emphasizing divine deliverance.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'deliverer' in Judges 3:9 can also mean what in the original language?
questions.correctAnswer: Savior or rescuer
questions.explanation: In Judges 3:9, the Hebrew word 'mashiach' (anointed one) or related root often means 'deliverer' or 'savior', highlighting God's raising of a rescuer like Othniel for Israel.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage shares the theme of God raising a deliverer when Israel cries out, similar to Judges 3?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 3:7-8
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:7-8 shows God hearing the affliction of His people and raising up a deliverer (Moses), paralleling the theme in Judges 3:9 where God raises Othniel and Ehud when Israel cries out.

questions.question: According to Judges 3, what sin caused the LORD to strengthen Eglon king of Moab against Israel?
options: Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 3:12 states Israel did evil, provoking the LORD to strengthen their enemy Eglon as punishment.

questions.question: True or False: After Ehud’s successful deliverance, the land had peace for forty years.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 3:30 states the land had rest for fourscore (eighty) years after Ehud’s deliverance, not forty.

questions.question: True or False: The narrative of Judges 3 demonstrates a repeated cycle of Israel's sin, oppression, crying out, and deliverance.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The whole chapter, including Judges 3:7-9 and 3:12-15, illustrates the cyclical pattern where Israel sins, is oppressed, cries out, and God raises a deliverer.

questions.question: Which king did the LORD sell Israel into the hands of because of their evil, before Ehud’s time?
questions.correctAnswer: Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia
questions.explanation: Judges 3:8 shows that after Israel’s evil, the LORD sold them into the hand of Chushanrishathaim king of Mesopotamia before Ehud’s era.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Judges 3:1, why did the LORD leave certain nations among the Israelites?
options: To punish Israel for their sins
To help Israel expand their territory
questions.correctAnswer: To prove Israel by them
questions.explanation: Judges 3:1 explicitly states that the LORD left these nations to prove Israel by them, testing those who had not known prior wars.

questions.question: What was the specific purpose of these nations being left among Israel according to Judges 3:2?
options: To teach Israel war to those who previously knew nothing of it
questions.correctAnswer: To teach Israel war to those who previously knew nothing of it
questions.explanation: Judges 3:2 reveals that the LORD intended these nations to help Israel learn war, especially the generations unfamiliar with it.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Judges 3:4 when Israel is tested by these nations?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in testing obedience
questions.explanation: Judges 3:4 shows God testing Israel to know if they will obey His commandments, reflecting His attribute of justice in holding His people accountable.

questions.question: What sin did Israel commit as described in Judges 3:6, leading to their downfall?
options: Intermarrying with foreign peoples and serving their gods
questions.correctAnswer: Intermarrying with foreign peoples and serving their gods
questions.explanation: Judges 3:6 states Israel took daughters of other nations as wives and served their gods, a direct violation of covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Israel’s repeated cycles of sin and deliverance in Judges 3:7-11?
options: The doctrine of repentance and divine deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of repentance and divine deliverance
questions.explanation: Judges 3:7-11 depicts Israel doing evil, being oppressed, crying out, and God raising a deliverer, illustrating repentance leading to salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is evidenced by God raising up Othniel as a deliverer in Judges 3:9-10?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty in raising judges
questions.explanation: Judges 3:9-10 reveals God's sovereign control in raising Othniel to deliver Israel when they repent, demonstrating His authority over history.

questions.question: How does Judges 3:12-14 continue the narrative arc of Israel’s relationship with God?
options: Israel sins again, God strengthens enemies to punish them, and Israel serves under oppression
Israel expands their territory freely without consequence
Israel remains faithful and is blessed
Israel builds a temple for Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Israel sins again, God strengthens enemies to punish them, and Israel serves under oppression
questions.explanation: Judges 3:12-14 shows Israel doing evil, God empowering Eglon to oppress them, continuing the cycle of sin and judgment in redemptive history.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by the fact that Ehud was left-handed and used this to deliver Israel in Judges 3:15-21?
options: God can use unexpected and unconventional means to accomplish His purposes
Only right-handed men are chosen by God
Physical strength is the key to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God can use unexpected and unconventional means to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Judges 3:15-21 presents Ehud’s left-handedness as a strategic advantage God uses, showing His sovereignty over human weakness and uniqueness.

questions.question: What synthesis of Judges 3:8 and Judges 3:15 reveals about God's response to Israel's sin?
options: God allows oppression as judgment but provides deliverance upon repentance
God immediately destroys all enemies without delay
God ignores Israel's cries for help
God punishes Israel without offering salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God allows oppression as judgment but provides deliverance upon repentance
questions.explanation: Judges 3:8 shows God giving Israel into oppression due to sin, and 3:15 shows God raising deliverers like Ehud when Israel cries out, illustrating judgment balanced with mercy.

questions.question: How does the account of Ehud’s killing of Eglon in Judges 3:21-25 foreshadow Christ’s work?
options: It typifies deliverance through a hidden, unexpected sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies deliverance through a hidden, unexpected sacrifice
questions.explanation: Ehud’s secret dagger and killing of Eglon foreshadows Christ’s unexpected sacrificial death that delivers God’s people from oppression and sin (Judges 3:21-25).

questions.question: What combined teaching do Judges 3:26-30 reveal about God’s deliverance and Israel’s obedience?
options: Deliverance is granted when Israel follows the lead of God’s appointed judge
Israel is saved by their own strength apart from God
God delivers Israel regardless of their faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Deliverance is granted when Israel follows the lead of God’s appointed judge
questions.explanation: Judges 3:26-30 shows Ehud leading Israel to victory, emphasizing that God’s deliverance coincides with Israel's obedience to His appointed leader.

questions.question: What theological implication about God's justice and mercy is drawn from Judges 3:7-8 and Judges 3:31?
options: God’s justice punishes sin, but His mercy raises deliverers to save
God is indifferent to Israel’s fate
God’s mercy means no consequences for sin
God’s justice is arbitrary and harsh
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice punishes sin, but His mercy raises deliverers to save
questions.explanation: Judges 3:7-8 shows punishment for sin, while 3:31 shows deliverance by Shamgar, illustrating the balance of God's justice and mercy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the cycle of sin and deliverance in Judges 3 demonstrates a capricious and uninvolved deity. What does Judges 3 actually teach about God's character?
options: God is just in punishing sin but merciful and sovereign in raising deliverers
God is absent and indifferent to human affairs
God is powerless to save Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God is just in punishing sin but merciful and sovereign in raising deliverers
questions.explanation: Judges 3 reveals God’s justice in allowing consequences for sin and His mercy in raising judges for deliverance, showing a deeply involved and righteous God (Judges 3:7-11, 15-16).

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching emerges from combining Judges 3:5-6 and Judges 3:7 about human sin nature and covenant unfaithfulness?
options: Human susceptibility to idolatry leads to covenant breach and divine judgment
Humans are naturally faithful to God
Sin does not affect the covenant relationship
questions.correctAnswer: Human susceptibility to idolatry leads to covenant breach and divine judgment
questions.explanation: Judges 3:5-6 shows Israel adopting foreign gods through marriage, and 3:7 indicates this leads to evil and forgetting God, revealing inherent sinfulness and covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Judges 3:11 and Judges 3:30 together illustrate the theme of divine rest after deliverance?
options: God grants periods of peace as a reward for obedience
God demands constant warfare without rest
Rest is unrelated to divine intervention
Rest only comes through human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God grants periods of peace as a reward for obedience
questions.explanation: Judges 3:11 and 3:30 both mention the land having rest after deliverance by judges, showing God’s blessing of peace tied to obedience and deliverance.
